text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj tells visiting vice president of Japan's parliament of his hope to see an increase of Japanese investments in Morocco.
- Five people sentenced to upto 10 years in jail for keeping some of the cocaine which has washed up on Morocco's Atlantic shores since June.
- Health workers union says first day of strike successful. Doctors and nurses started a three-day stoppage on Tuesday.
- Low spending in publicity sector with only 0.25 percent of Gross Domestic Product.
- Morocco launches $106 million free trade zone near the northern city of Tangier.
- Interior Minister Driss Basri asks voters to pick up their cards for July 25 elections of professional chambers.
- Authorities refuse to authorise peaceful march planned by health sector workers on Wednesday in Rabat.
